sentence_stem: Whoever had drafted the original proposal
correct_completion: clearly understood the importance of public trust.
full_sentence: Whoever had drafted the original proposal clearly understood the importance of public trust.
acceptable_variants: clearly grasped why public trust mattered.
knew perfectly well how important public trust was.

options.text: to clearly understand the importance of public trust.
options.why_wrong: An infinitive cannot serve as the finite verb of the subject clause 'whoever had drafted'.

options.text: the importance of public trust was clear.
options.why_wrong: This introduces a new subject, leaving the nominal clause without a predicate that fits it.

options.text: clearly understood the importance of public trust.
understanding the importance of public trust.
options.why_wrong: A participle cannot act as the main predicate of the sentence, so the subject clause remains unfinished.

grammar_focus: Free relative (nominal) clause 'whoever ...' functioning as the subject
explanation: A nominal clause introduced by 'whoever' functions as the subject of the sentence, so the main clause needs a finite verb that agrees with it. Here 'clearly understood' provides that predicate.
